summary: Kiyoshi Yabuuchi was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University from 1926 to 1929. He held posts at Kyoto University (circa 1935–1969) and Ryukoku University (circa 1970–1977).

Kiyotaka Kimura, active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology, studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1983–2001) and Tsurumi Women's University (circa 2001–2011).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held academic posts at Hokkaido University (circa 1993–2004), Tohoku University (circa 2004–2021), and Toyo Bunko.

Kiyozo Kazama worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He held posts at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.

Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring. He served as professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991/1994.

Klaus Butzenberger specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm. He worked at the University of Munich, Free University of Berlin, and Humboldt University, then held a chair at the University of Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Karttunen specializes in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics, having studied at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola, among others. His career included roles at the Academy of Finland and the University of Helsinki.

Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt under Paul Thieme, and Tübingen. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (circa 1955–1959) and the University of Cologne as an ordinary professor (1963–1987).

Klaus Mylius worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Leipzig, and held teaching posts at Halle-Wittenberg, the University of Leipzig (1970–1991), University of Bayreuth, University of Göttingen, and Goethe University Frankfurt.
Klaus Pinte specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and held a postdoctoral teaching post there in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn, a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, linguistic, and Buddhist studies, studied at Leipzig, Hamburg, and Giessen. He held posts at the University of Giessen and served as ordinary professor of Turkology at the University of Göttingen (1992–2003).
Klaus Rüping was an Indologist who studied under Paul Hacker and held an academic post at the University of Münster (attested 1978).

Klaus Wille is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997) and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2026).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Marburg and Hamburg, studying under Klaus Sagaster and Michael Hahn, and held positions at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, University of Hamburg, and University of Vienna.

Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Philosophisch-Theologische Hochschule Benediktbeuern and the University of Munich, where he later served as a lecturer in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Uppsala University by 2000 under the supervision of Peter Schalk.

Knut A. Jacobsen works in religious studies and Indology, earning his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara. He held professorships at the University of Bergen starting in 1996 and at the University of Oslo circa 1996.

Kobun Otogawa was a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, and Eihei-ji. He held posts at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center, Haiku Zendo, and Naropa University.

Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari, and at Komazawa University. He held multiple leadership posts at Komazawa University between 1892 and 1909 and lectured at the University of Tokyo.
Kodo Kawamura specialized in Buddhist studies. He completed his graduate and doctoral studies at Komazawa University, where he also served as a professor from circa 1968 to 2004.
